summary: This resolution amends House Rule XXIII to bar Members, officers, and employees from entering prediction-market contracts or swaps on event outcomes (excluding insurance and sports wagers) and expresses the sense that the executive and judicial branches should adopt similar restrictions.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends House ethics rules to prohibit Members and staff from participating in certain prediction markets. It contains no provisions related to government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.
The bill addresses internal House rules on prediction market trading and has no provisions concerning tax rates, tax policy, or revenue collection.
No content in the bill relates to healthcare systems, insurance, or medical policy.
The legislation is unrelated to firearms regulations or Second Amendment issues.
The bill makes no reference to immigration, border policy, or citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
The resolution contains nothing about military funding or defense policy.
No environmental or climate-related measures are present.
The bill does not engage with welfare programs or social safety net policies.
No education policy, school funding, or related provisions appear in the text.
The legislation is silent on drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No criminal justice reforms, sentencing, or policing measures are included.
The bill does not address trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
Nothing in the resolution concerns deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The text contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No foreign aid or international assistance measures are mentioned.

While prediction markets may sometimes involve election outcomes, the bill solely imposes ethics restrictions on House personnel trading and does not alter voting access, election procedures, or integrity standards.
The resolution does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No labor, union, or employment rights provisions are present.
The bill makes no reference to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
